name: Apple Silicon unified memory enables 70B+ model execution on consumer devices, but autoregressive decode speed is strictly bounded by LPDDR package bandwidth
symptom: Practitioners purchasing 64GB-128GB Macs frequently expect high decode throughput for 70B models based on the large unified pool, but observe single-user batch-1 decode speeds of only 8-15 tokens/second, which feels underwhelming compared to multi-GPU enterprise setups.
root_cause: Single-batch LLM decode is strictly memory-bandwidth bound: generating each token requires streaming every model parameter from memory into compute cores. Apple Silicon integrates high-capacity LPDDR5/LPDDR5X on-package to maintain battery-friendly power consumption (~30-60W package power), but its absolute bandwidth ceiling is verified from Apple technical specifications as: M4 Pro at 273 GB/s, M3 Max at 300 or 400 GB/s, M4 Max at 410 or 546 GB/s, and M1/M3 Ultra at 800 or 819 GB/s. For a 70B parameter model in 4-bit precision (~35 GB weights), the theoretical maximum decode roofline is bandwidth / weight_bytes: on M4 Pro (273 GB/s), max theoretical is 7.8 tok/s; on M3 Max (400 GB/s), max is 11.4 tok/s; on M4 Max (546 GB/s), max is 15.6 tok/s; and on M3 Ultra (819 GB/s), max is 23.4 tok/s. Achieved throughput is typically 75-85% of this physical roofline.
workaround: Accept that Apple Silicon's primary advantage is capacity per dollar and power efficiency (running 70B locally on ~50W), not peak decode speed. To improve tokens/sec, employ speculative decoding (such as draft models, MTP, or DFlash) to amortize weight bandwidth across multiple generated tokens per pass, or quantize to 3-bit / 4-bit formats rather than 8-bit / fp16.
notes: Verified against Apple's official tech specs: M4 Pro (273 GB/s, support.apple.com/en-us/121553), M3 Max (400 GB/s, support.apple.com/en-us/117737), M4 Max (546 GB/s, support.apple.com/en-us/122211), M1 Ultra (800 GB/s, support.apple.com/en-us/111900), and M3 Ultra (819 GB/s, support.apple.com/en-us/122211). Contrast with discrete datacenter cards: NVIDIA H100 SXM offers 3,350 GB/s (HBM3) and RTX 5090 offers 1,792 GB/s (GDDR7), yielding 3x-6x higher decode rates but with strict 24-32 GB capacity limits on consumer cards.
